extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to Cambridge University Press / Cambridge Core journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on composing Data Availability Statements (DAS) for journal manuscripts, including what to say about availability, where to place the statement, and example wording for common availability statuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Data Availability Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Availability Statements are brief statements about whether the authors of an article have made the evidence supporting their findings available, and if so, where readers may access it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They’re not just for quantitative data – they can also be used to describe evidence such as qualitative materials and “data” in the broadest sense. DAS help to promote transparency and reproducibility and increase the visibility of evidence produced during research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include a DAS
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of our commitment to supporting open research, some of our journals now require all manuscripts to include a Data Availability Statement in order to be accepted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check your chosen journal’s instructions for authors for any additional or mandatory requirements related to sharing data or other evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core content: state availability and access details
rubrics_metrics.description: A Data Availability Statement simply needs to state whether you have made evidence available, and if so, where and how it can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You do not have to make all data publicly available; the statement must at minimum report availability status and provide access information (e.g., repository name, URL, DOI, contact details).

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as 'data'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Data" is interpreted in the broadest sense to mean any evidence or resources that would be necessary for others to fully evaluate the basis for your findings, and to verify or reproduce your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes raw or processed data sets, code, protocols, and qualitative resources such as images, audio, video, maps, interview transcripts, field notes, public reports, and any information necessary for others to access, interpret and process these resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of the Data Availability Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Availability Statements should generally be placed in the back matter of your manuscript, just before your References, unless your chosen journal specifies otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the journal’s specified location if it differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling DAS under double-blind peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: If your journal uses a double-blind peer review process, it's important to ensure that the information in your Data Availability Statement doesn't compromise the anonymity of you or your co-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is identifying information in the DAS, submit it the same way as you would any other identifying information associated with your manuscript (for example, as part of a Title Page or as a separate document) according to the journal’s instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow journal-specific data sharing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If your chosen journal has additional requirements related to sharing data or other evidence, these will be specified in the journal’s instructions for authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the journal or openresearch@cambrige.org (as listed) if you have questions about specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data openly available in a public repository (example wording)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example template: 'The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in [repository name] at http://doi.org/[doi], reference number [reference number].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the repository name and a permanent identifier (such as a DOI) or stable URL to allow readers to retrieve the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data embargoed due to commercial restrictions (example wording)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example template: 'The data that support the findings of this study will be available in [repository name] at [URL / DOI link] following a [6 month] embargo from the date of publication, to allow for commercialisation of research findings.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the duration and reason for the embargo and where the data will be deposited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data available on request due to privacy/ethical restrictions (example wording)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example template: 'The data that support the findings of this study are available on request from the corresponding author, [initials]. The data are not publicly available due to [restrictions e.g. their containing information that could compromise the privacy of research participants].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the contact (e.g., corresponding author initials) and the reason for non-public availability (privacy, ethics), so readers know how to request access and why public sharing is restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data generated at a central facility, available on request (example wording)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example template: 'Raw data were generated at [facility name]. Derived data supporting the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author [initials] on request.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the facility where raw data were produced and clarify what derived data are available and how to request them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data subject to third-party restrictions (example wording)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example template: 'The data that support the findings of this study are available from [third party]. Restrictions apply to the availability of these data, which were used under licence for this study. Data are available [from the authors / at URL] with the permission of [third party].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly indicate the third party controlling access, the nature of the restrictions, and the process for obtaining permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data available within the article or supplementary materials (example wording)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example template: 'The authors confirm that the data supporting the findings of this study are available within the article [and/or its supplementary materials].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all necessary evidence is included in the article or its supplements, state this explicitly so readers know where to find it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing not applicable – no new data generated (example wording)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example template: 'Data availability is not applicable to this article as no new data were created or analysed in this study.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this statement only when truly no original data were generated or analysed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data available on request from the authors (reasonable request) (example wording)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example template: 'The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author, [author initials], upon reasonable request.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the contact and that access is subject to a reasonable request; if there are any conditions or processes for fulfilling requests, indicate them.
